hook: Don't expect a standard report: the whole file is staged as a question-and-answer exchange between a Reader and a Narrator, and that format is part of the anomaly. Every question is asked twice, which feels odd at first and then settles into a rhythm. It is short, dry and quietly funny, and some familiarity with Greek myth and classical philosophy goes a long way.
whyItMatters: SCP-4500 sits in the 4000 series and is tagged concept and meta, the kind of article that plays with how SCP documents are written as much as with what they describe. Here the joke is that the containment procedures themselves require the dialogue form. Choosing a Platonic ideal as its subject lets it borrow philosophical vocabulary for things like task forces and clearance tests.
thingsToNotice:
The rooms turn out to be an ancient Greek forerunner of the Foundation, once sited near Athens, whose files survive as ideal dialogues, and the examples recast myth as containment paperwork. Pandora breaks the seal on a stasis jar during routine testing and only one escapee is ever recaptured; Pythagoras finds irrational numbers, which are handled as a spreading idea, with outsiders who know of them drowned at sea; a hundred-headed, fire-breathing father of monsters is kept in a pit while Scholar Zeus throws thunderbolts at every tremor. Notice the threat ranks of Iron, Silver and Gold in place of the modern classes.

Example 4 is the twist hiding in plain sight. Its designation reads Pi Lambda Alpha, it is not a threat but a last resort, and it is described as breaking chains and walking out of the cave into the light, which explains how the whole facility left the material world for the realm of ideals, apparently because every other constraint failed. Then the file closes on Herakles' empty room with its straw bed, where the only note is that after Megara's death his rash behavior earned him duty guarding the Gold-rank horrors; it is the shortest entry and the most human one.
